     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.

    '/api/update-assignment-progress',
    '/api/cancel-journey',
    '/api/reroute-journey',
    '/api/split-journey',
    '/api/merge-journeys',
    '/api/edit-active-plan',
    '/api/report-disruption',
    '/api/configure-capacity',
    '/api/set-location-status',
    '/api/set-worker-availability',
    '/api/update-sample-type',
    '/api/update-location',
    '/api/authenticate-user',
    '/api/select-active-role',
    '/api/create-user',
    '/api/update-user-access',
    '/api/read-user/{userId}',
    '/api/create-collection-request',
    '/api/ingest-presealed-sample',
    '/api/check-serviceability',
    '/api/read-serviceability-snapshot',
    '/api/list-role-work',
    '/api/read-sample-state/{sampleId}',
    '/api/read-sample-lifecycle',
    '/api/read-journey-plan',
    '/api/read-operations-state',
    '/api/events',
]
for p in paths_of_interest:
    path = d['paths'].get(p)
    if not path:
        print('MISSING PATH', p)
        continue
    for method, op in path.items():
        print(f'\n===== {method.upper()} {p}  op={op.get("operationId")}')
        req = op.get('requestBody')
        if req:
            schema = req['content']['application/json']['schema']
            print('REQ required:', schema.get('required'))
            print('REQ props:', list(schema.get('properties', {}).keys()))
        for code, resp in op.get('responses', {}).items():
            content = resp.get('content', {}).get('application/json', {}).get('schema')
            if content:
                print(f'RESP {code}:', json.dumps(content)[:800])
PY

import json
with open('/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json') as f:

# remaining endpoints
for p in [
    '/api/check-serviceability',
    '/api/read-serviceability-snapshot',
    '/api/create-sample-type',
    '/api/create-connection',
    '/api/set-connection-status',
    '/api/set-location-function-status',
    '/api/configure-laboratory-acceptance',
    '/api/read-sample-lifecycle',
    '/api/read-journey-plan',
    '/api/list-role-work',
    '/api/events',
    '/api/search-audit-trail',
    '/api/collect-and-seal-sample',
    '/api/confirm-laboratory-receipt',
    '/api/record-worker-location',
    '/api/update-assignment-progress',
    '/api/initiate-handoff',
    '/api/confirm-handoff',
    '/api/record-handling-checkpoint',
    '/api/record-laboratory-exception',
    '/api/reroute-journey',
    '/api/cancel-journey',
    '/ready',
]:
    path = d['paths'].get(p)
    if not path:
        print('MISSING', p); continue
    for method, op in path.items():
        print(f'\n===== {method.upper()} {p}  op={op.get("operationId")}')
        req = op.get('requestBody')
        if req:
            schema = req['content']['application/json']['schema']
            print('REQ required:', schema.get('required'))
            print('REQ props:', list(schema.get('properties', {}).keys()))
            print('REQ addl:', schema.get('additionalProperties'))

     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
    97	
    98	## Collection requests
    99	
   100	A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:
   101	
   102	- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
   103	- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
   104	- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
   105	- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.
   106	
   107	The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.
   108	
   109	## Pre-sealed samples
   110	
   111	A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.
   112	
   113	- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
   114	- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.
   115	
   116	## Sample types
   117	
   118	Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.
   119	
   120	- **Amber** — standard handling.
   121	- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
   122	- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
   123	- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.
   124	
   125	These named rules are in addition to the generic handling attributes (container, temperature range, qualified-collector requirement, and incompatibilities).
   126	
   127	## Network locations
   128	
   129	The transport network is made up of locations. A single location — a node — may act as a collection point, a transfer point, a hub, a laboratory, or any combination of these (for example, a hub that also acts as a laboratory).
   130	
   131	- **Collection point** — where samples are collected from or enter the network. Serviceability is measured from active collection points.
   132	- **Transfer point / hub** — where a sample changes custody or moves between transport legs.
   133	- **Laboratory** — where a sample is received and its journey completes; a laboratory accepts specific sample types.
   134	
   135	A location may perform several of these functions at the same time.
   136	
   137	## Journey and assignment rules
   138	
   139	The system must support direct, multi-stop and batched journeys.
   140	
   141	A journey may contain several separately assigned transport legs. For example:
   142	
   143	1. Patient’s home to a local collection centre
   144	2. Local collection centre to a hub
   145	3. Hub to the laboratory
   146	
   147	Each movement between two locations is a separate assignment and may be handled by a different worker.
   148	
   149	Collection must happen before transport. Pickup must happen before delivery, and responsibility for the sample must be transferred through a confirmed handoff before the next person continues the journey.
   150

USER_CONTEXT: Implement Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts exactly. Clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing first, then may pass through relay couriers, centres, and hubs. Handoffs require dual confirmation; sender remains responsible until both sides confirm; no duplicate custody transfers. All custody changes appear in sample history.

TASK_TRACKING:
- Inspect remaining handlers/frontend/OpenAPI to lock payload shapes (in progress → nearly complete)
- Align backend response payloads to OpenAPI schemas (pending, next)
- Implement missing frontend (App.tsx + views) against UI contract (pending)
- Wire app-setup (pending; /workspace/app-setup is empty)

COMPLETED:
- Read backend: handlers.go (~1347 lines), handlers_ops.go (handoff/accept/journey/capacity), planning.go (route search), db.go (seed types, store), models.go (roles/types), main.go (App/server), http.go (auth/errors), audit.go
- Read frontend stubs: api.ts (roles + ApiError), main.tsx, styles.css, vite.config.ts (proxy /api+/ready → :8080), index.html, package.json (maplibre-gl 5.24.0, pmtiles, react 19)
- Read contracts: openapi.contract.json ops (accept/decline_assignment, collect_and_seal, initiate/confirm_handoff, lab receipt/exception, create/update/read user, sample types, set_worker_availability); ui.contract.json scenarios (login, role switch, work view, sample history/freshness/custodian)
- Read map-assets/style.json (Offline Bangalore Light, center 77.5946,12.9716)
- Catalogued handler funcs across handlers.go, handlers_ops.go, planning.go, db.go

PENDING:
- Lock remaining backend payloads to OpenAPI (user/sample-type/assignment/handoff/journey/lab shapes)
- Build frontend App.tsx + role work views matching UI contract scenarios
- Implement /workspace/app-setup wiring
- Verify dual-confirm handoff, no duplicate custody, history on every transfer

CURRENT_STATE:
- Agent has "clear picture of contract gaps"; next action is payload lock then frontend
- Role name mismatch to watch: backend collection_professional / delivery_partner vs frontend certified_collection_professional / relay_courier
- Seeded sample type "Amber" (qualified collector, 2–30C, no cooled route)

     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42

    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52

USER_CONTEXT: Implement Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts exactly. Clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing first, then may pass through relay couriers, centres, and hubs. Handoffs require dual confirmation; sender remains responsible until both sides confirm; no duplicate custody transfers. All custody changes appear in sample history.

TASK_TRACKING:
- Inspect remaining backend/frontend/app-setup files and lock API/UI to contracts (IN_PROGRESS)
- Align backend payloads, role names, error envelopes to OpenAPI schemas (IN_PROGRESS)
- Build frontend around pinned UI contract scenarios (PENDING)
- Finish app-setup (PENDING)

COMPLETED:
- Inspected backend: main.go, handlers.go, handlers_ops.go, db.go, models.go, planning.go, http.go
- Inspected frontend skeleton: src/api.ts, main.tsx, styles.css, package.json, index.html, vite.config.ts
- Inspected contracts: openapi.contract.json (Role, ErrorEnvelope, OperationsState, LocationFunctionStates, collect-and-seal, location/connection status endpoints), ui.contract.json (scenarios)
- Confirmed map assets at /opt/arena/map-assets (bangalore.pmtiles)
- Identified remaining contract mismatches in backend payloads vs OpenAPI schemas

PENDING:
- Lock backend JSON payloads/role names to OpenAPI contract
- Implement full frontend matching UI contract scenarios (login, role switch, sample views, freshness, location/custodian)
- App-setup remaining work

CURRENT_STATE:
- Backend is a Go service (App + Store) with Postgres/Mongo, bcrypt auth, uuid IDs
- Roles in frontend api.ts: requester, certified_collection_professional, relay_courier, node_handler, laboratory_intake_operator, dispatcher, administrator
- Key handlers: handleAccept, handleOpsState, handleEditPlan, handleLabException, handleReady, location/function/connection status, create-sample-type
- Models: Sample (ID, RequestID, RequesterID, OriginLat/Lng/Type/NodeID, RequestedAt...), APIError {error, code}, Coordinate {latitude, longitude}
- Timeouts: OfferTimeout=5m, NoWorkerTimeout=15m, StaleLocationAge=5m, DeclinePenalty=30m
- Frontend: Vite+React 19, maplibre-gl 5.24.0, pmtiles 4.4.1, react-router-dom; proxy /api and /ready to :8080
- UI contract product: lab-sample-pickup-and-delivery; scenarios include login_rejects_invalid_credentials, role_switch_control_lists_and_applies_role, role_work_view_shows_current_and_past, sample_view_shows_ordered_status_history, sample_freshness_visible_to_owner, sample_view_shows_location_custodian
- Frontend src currently has only api.ts, main.tsx, styles.css — App.tsx and feature views not yet present
- sampleStatePayload in handlers_ops.go builds history/assignments/legs for sample views
- Location function updates bump network revision and rebuild serviceability snapshot

CODE_STATE:

- /workspace/frontend/src/{api.ts,main.tsx,styles.css} — App component imported but not listed in src
- /workspace/contracts/{openapi.contract.json,ui.contract.json}
- /workspace/INSTRUCTION.md describes domain rules

DEPS:

- Frontend: react 19, react-dom, react-router-dom, maplibre-gl, pmtiles, vite

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.

---README---
# Public task inputs

The candidate receives the frozen API contract and UI contract in this directory. Evaluator-only
files remain outside `tasks/public/`.
---INSTRUCTION first 50---
# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System

Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.

Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.

Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.

Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.

## Users and responsibilities

Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.

For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.

A user may have more than one assigned role:

- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.

### Requester

A requester should be able to:

- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
- Create a home or clinic collection request.
- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
- See only requests that belong to them.

The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.

### Certified collection professional

A certified collection professional should be able to:

- View collection work for which they are qualified.
- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
- Record their current location.
- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.

### Relay courier

A relay courier should be able to:

- View delivery work assigned to them.
- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
- Record location and progress updates.

Clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing first, then may pass through relay couriers, centres, and hubs. Handoffs require dual confirmation; sender remains responsible until both sides confirm; no duplicate custody transfers. All custody changes appear in sample history.

TASK_TRACKING:
- Inspect remaining contract mismatches and lock backend payloads/status codes to pinned OpenAPI schemas (IN PROGRESS)
- Build frontend views matching UI contract scenarios (PENDING)
- Implement app-setup (PENDING)

COMPLETED:
- Inspected OpenAPI schemas: Role, SampleState, RoleWork, RoleWorkItem, RoleWorkSampleItem, RoleWorkAssignmentItem, SampleWorkItem, JourneyWorkItem, AssignmentWorkItem, OperationsState, AuditSearchResult, AuditEntry, JourneyPlan, JourneyStop, JourneyLeg, SampleLifecycle, RequesterJourneyPlan, Worker schemas
- Inspected backend: handlers.go, handlers_ops.go (sampleStatePayload, handleCancelJourney), models.go (roles, Capacity.fillAvail), db.go, audit.go, planning.go, schema.sql, http.go, main.go
- Inspected frontend skeleton: api.ts (Role types already match contract), main.tsx, styles.css, package.json (React 19, Vite, maplibre-gl 5.24.0, pmtiles 4.4.1)
- Inspected UI contract scenarios: login_rejects_invalid_credentials, role_switch_control_lists_and_applies_role, role_work_view_shows_current_and_past, sample_view_shows_ordered_status_history, sample_freshnes...
- Confirmed frontend/src has only api.ts, main.tsx, styles.css — App.tsx and views missing
- Confirmed app-setup/ is empty
- Confirmed map assets at /opt/arena/map-assets/style.json (Offline Bangalore Light, pmtiles)

PENDING:
- Lock remaining backend payloads and status codes to OpenAPI schemas
- Build missing frontend (App.tsx + role/sample/ops views matching UI scenarios)
- Implement app-setup

CURRENT_STATE:
- Backend exists with roles: administrator, dispatcher, requester, collection_professional, delivery_partner, node_handler (models.go); frontend api.ts uses certified_collection_professional, relay_courier, laboratory_intake_operator — role-name mismatch still open
- Frontend is a skeleton only (no App.tsx); app-setup empty
- Map: Offline Bangalore Light via pmtiles at /map-assets/bangalore.pmtiles
- Agent next step: lock backend payloads then build frontend and app-setup

 '/api/merge-journeys','/api/edit-active-plan','/api/report-disruption','/api/read-journey-plan',
 '/api/read-sample-lifecycle','/api/read-sample-state/{sampleId}','/api/read-operations-state',
 '/api/list-role-work','/api/set-worker-availability','/api/configure-capacity',
 '/api/configure-laboratory-acceptance','/api/set-location-function-status','/api/set-location-status',
 '/api/set-connection-status','/api/create-connection','/api/create-location','/api/update-location',
 '/api/create-sample-type','/api/update-sample-type','/api/create-user','/api/update-user-access',
 '/api/read-user/{userId}','/ready'
]
for p in paths_of_interest:
    op=spec['paths'].get(p)
    if not op:
        print('MISSING PATH', p)
        continue
    method=list(op.keys())[0]
    body=op[method].get('requestBody',{})
    print('\n========', method.upper(), p, 'op=', op[method].get('operationId'))

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
    97	
    98	## Collection requests
    99	
   100	A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:
   101	
   102	- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
   103	- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
   104	- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
   105	- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.
   106	
   107	The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.
   108	
   109	## Pre-sealed samples
   110	
   111	A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.
   112	
   113	- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
   114	- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.
   115	
   116	## Sample types
   117	
   118	Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.
   119	
   120	- **Amber** — standard handling.
   121	- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
   122	- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
   123	- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.
   124	
   125	These named rules are in addition to the generic handling attributes (container, temperature range, qualified-collector requirement, and incompatibilities).
   126	
   127	## Network locations
   128	
   129	The transport network is made up of locations. A single location — a node — may act as a collection point, a transfer point, a hub, a laboratory, or any combination of these (for example, a hub that also acts as a laboratory).
   130	
   131	- **Collection point** — where samples are collected from or enter the network. Serviceability is measured from active collection points.
   132	- **Transfer point / hub** — where a sample changes custody or moves between transport legs.
   133	- **Laboratory** — where a sample is received and its journey completes; a laboratory accepts specific sample types.
   134	
   135	A location may perform several of these functions at the same time.
   136	
   137	## Journey and assignment rules
   138	
   139	The system must support direct, multi-stop and batched journeys.
   140	
   141	A journey may contain several separately assigned transport legs. For example:
   142	
   143	1. Patient’s home to a local collection centre
   144	2. Local collection centre to a hub
   145	3. Hub to the laboratory
   146	
   147	Each movement between two locations is a separate assignment and may be handled by a different worker.
   148	
   149	Collection must happen before transport. Pickup must happen before delivery, and responsibility for the sample must be transferred through a confirmed handoff before the next person continues the journey.

     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.

    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.

import json
p='/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json'
with open(p) as f:
    spec=json.load(f)

want = [
 'check_serviceability','create_collection_request','ingest_presealed_sample',
 'collect_and_seal_sample','initiate_handoff','confirm_handoff',
 'confirm_laboratory_receipt','record_laboratory_exception','record_handling_checkpoint',
 'record_worker_location','update_assignment_progress','list_role_work','read_sample_state',
 'read_sample_lifecycle','read_journey_plan','read_operations_state','read_ui_bootstrap',
 'search_audit_trail','reroute_journey','split_journey','merge_journeys',
 'edit_active_plan','report_disruption','read_serviceability_snapshot','create_location',
 'set_location_status','set_location_function_status','create_connection',
 'set_connection_status','configure_capacity','configure_laboratory_acceptance',
 'set_worker_availability','create_sample_type','read_user','select_active_role'
]
for path, methods in spec['paths'].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        if m.startswith('x-'): continue
        oid=op.get('operationId')
        if oid not in want: continue
        print('\n', '='*80)
        print(f'{m.upper()} {path}  {oid}')
        rb=op.get('requestBody',{})
        if rb:
            sch=rb.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema')
            if isinstance(sch, dict):
                print('  REQ required:', sch.get('required'))
                print('  REQ props:', list(sch.get('properties',{}).keys()))
        for code in ['200','201']:
            resp = op.get('responses',{}).get(code)
            if not resp: continue
            sch=resp.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema')
            if not sch: 
                print(f'  RESP {code}: no schema')
                continue
            d=sch.get('properties',{}).get('data',{})
            if '$ref' in d:
                print(f'  RESP {code} data $ref {d["$ref"]}')
            else:
                print(f'  RESP {code} data required: {d.get("required")}')
                print(f'  RESP {code} data props: {list(d.get("properties",{}).keys())}')
                print(f'  RESP {code} data addl: {d.get("additionalProperties")}')
                # print nested property types briefly
                for k,v in d.get('properties',{}).items():
                    if '$ref' in v:
                        print(f'      {k}: $ref {v["$ref"]}')
                    elif v.get('type')=='array':
                        it=v.get('items',{})
                        print(f'      {k}: array of {it.get("$ref") or it.get("type")}')
                    elif v.get('enum'):
                        print(f'      {k}: enum {v["enum"]}')
                    else:
                        print(f'      {k}: {v.get("type")}')
        # error codes for 400/409
        for code in ['400','403','409']:
            resp = op.get('responses',{}).get(code)
            if not resp: continue
            sch=resp.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema')
            if sch and 'code' in sch.get('properties',{}):
                print(f'  {code} codes:', sch['properties']['code'].get('enum'))

        # error codes for 400/409
        for code in ['400','403','409']:
            resp = op.get('responses',{}).get(code)

            sch=resp.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema')

Clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing first, then may pass through relay couriers, centres, and hubs. Handoffs need dual confirmation; sender stays responsible until both confirm; no duplicate custody transfers. All custody changes appear in sample history. Schemas are strict.

- backend-openapi-alignment: IN_PROGRESS — lock payloads/status codes to OpenAPI schemas (SampleLifecycle, RequesterJourneyPlan, WorkerJourneyPlan, ServiceabilityRegion, RealtimeEvent, LocationFunction, Role, RoleWork, SampleState, JourneyPlan, TimelineEntry, Capacity, ErrorEnvelope, AuditSearchResult, etc.)

# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System

Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.

Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.

Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.

Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.

## Users and responsibilities

Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.

For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.

A user may have more than one assigned role:

- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.

### Requester

A requester should be able to:

- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
- Create a home or clinic collection request.
- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
- See only requests that belong to them.

The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.

### Certified collection professional

A certified collection professional should be able to:

- View collection work for which they are qualified.
- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
- Record their current location.
- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.

### Relay courier

A relay courier should be able to:

- View delivery work assigned to them.
- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
- Record location and progress updates.
- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.

### Node handler

A node handler should be able to:

- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.

### Laboratory intake operator

A laboratory intake operator should be able to:

- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
- Confirm that a sample was received.
- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.

### Dispatcher

A dispatcher should be able to:

- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.

python3 - <<'PY'
import json
p='/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json'
with open(p) as f:
    spec=json.load(f)
s=spec['components']['schemas']

for name in ['RoleWork','OperationsState','LocationFunctionStates','Certification','Coordinate']:
    print('\n=======', name, '=======')
    print(json.dumps(s[name], indent=2)[:4000])

# remaining response schemas
for path, methods in spec['paths'].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        if m.startswith('x-'): continue
        oid=op.get('operationId')
        for code, resp in op.get('responses',{}).items():
            if not str(code).startswith('2'): continue
            sch=resp.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema')
            if not sch: continue
            data=sch.get('properties',{}).get('data',{})
            print(f'\n--- {oid} {m.upper()} {path} {code} ---')
            if '$ref' in data:
                print('data $ref', data['$ref'])
            elif data.get('oneOf'):
                print('data oneOf', data['oneOf'])
            else:
                print('required', data.get('required'))
                print('props', list(data.get('properties',{}).keys()))
                print('addl', data.get('additionalProperties'))
                # print nested briefly
                for k,v in data.get('properties',{}).items():
                    extra=''
                    if '$ref' in v: extra=' ref '+v['$ref']
                    elif v.get('allOf'): extra=' allOf'
                    elif v.get('enum'): extra=' enum '+str(v['enum'])
                    elif v.get('type')=='array': extra=' [] '+str(v.get('items',{}).get('$ref') or v.get('items',{}).get('type'))
                    else: extra=' '+str(v.get('type'))
                    print(f'  {k}:{extra}')
PY

The backend exists and is fairly complete, but many response payloads don't match the OpenAPI contract exactly (additionalProperties: false on most schemas). I need to:

2. Build frontend to match UI contract scenarios
3. Implement app-setup

Key payload mismatches I identified:

**Role names**: Backend uses:
- collection_professional
- delivery_partner
- laboratory_team

OpenAPI Role enum:
- collection_professional
- delivery_partner
- laboratory_team

Wait, the OpenAPI Role schema says:
`['administrator', 'dispatcher', 'requester', 'collection_professional', 'delivery_partner', 'node_handler', 'laboratory_team']`

But the frontend/api.ts uses:
- certified_collection_professional
- relay_courier
- laboratory_intake_operator

And the user task description uses those longer names. The PINNED OpenAPI contract uses the shorter names. I MUST follow the OpenAPI contract exactly.

The UI contract uses accessible-role-label-visible-text strategy. The UI should display human-readable labels like "Certified collection professional" while sending the API role values.

**sampleStatePayload** currently includes extra fields not in SampleState schema:
SampleState required: sampleId, requestId, requesterId, origin, originType, requestedAt, deliveryDeadline, sampleTypeId, containerType, temperatureMinC, temperatureMaxC, incompatibleSampleTypes, serviceability, activeAssignmentIds, state, timeline, locationStale
Optional: activeJourneyId, targetLaboratoryId, latestLocation, locationRecordedAt

Current payload has extras: status, sealed, serviceabilityReason, earliestCollectionAt, latestCollectionAt, freshness, history, legs, alreadySealed, currentHolderId, currentCustodianId, currentCustodian, currentLocation, lastLocationAt, lastUpdatedAt, journeyId, routeProgress, exception, sealedAt

These extra fields will FAIL additionalProperties: false validation.

**sampleLifecycle** current: `{sampleId, events, history}` - missing required fields.

**journeyPayload** needs to match JourneyPlan / RequesterJourneyPlan / WorkerJourneyPlan depending on role.

**operations state** needs: samples, workers, locations, connections, routes, handoffs, delays, exceptions (required). Current has collectionNodes, laboratories, wrong sample/worker shapes.

**bootstrap** needs: user (with roleSelectionRequired), serverTime. Current has extra sampleTypes, locations, map - additionalProperties: false so extras will fail.

**Location schema** for create/update location - need to check Location schema.

**Various operation responses** with extra fields or missing required fields.

Let me get more details on remaining schemas and current handler responses.

import json
p='/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json'
with open(p) as f:
    spec=json.load(f)
print('======= COMPONENTS SCHEMAS =======')
for name, schema in spec.get('components',{}).get('schemas',{}).items():
    print(f'\n======= {name} =======')
    print(json.dumps(schema, indent=2)[:1800])
print('\n======= remaining success schemas =======')
for path, methods in spec['paths'].items():
    for method, op in methods.items():
        oid=op.get('operationId')
        for code, resp in op.get('responses',{}).items():
            if not str(code).startswith('2') and code != '101':
                continue
            schema=resp.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema')
            if not schema:
                print(f'{oid} {code}: no json schema')
                continue
            data=schema.get('properties',{}).get('data', schema)
            print(f'\n======= {oid} {code} =======')
            print(json.dumps(data, indent=2)[:2200])
PY

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.

import json
p="/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json"
with open(p) as f:
    d=json.load(f)

# dump each operation's request required fields and 200/201 data schema required+properties
for path, methods in d["paths"].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        if m.startswith("x-"): continue
        oid=op.get("operationId")
        print("="*80)
        print(f"{m.upper()} {path}  {oid}")
        rb=op.get("requestBody")
        if rb:
            content=rb.get("content",{}).get("application/json",{})
            sch=content.get("schema",{})
            print("  REQUEST required:", sch.get("required"))
            print("  REQUEST props:", list(sch.get("properties",{}).keys()))
            print("  additionalProperties:", sch.get("additionalProperties"))
        params=op.get("parameters")
        if params:
            print("  PARAMS:", [(p.get("name"), p.get("in"), p.get("required")) for p in params])
        for code in ["200","201","204"]:
            resp=op.get("responses",{}).get(code)
            if not resp: continue
            sch=resp.get("content",{}).get("application/json",{}).get("schema",{})
            if not sch: 
                print(f"  {code}: no schema")
                continue
            data=sch.get("properties",{}).get("data", sch)
            print(f"  {code} required:", data.get("required") if isinstance(data,dict) else data)
            if isinstance(data,dict):
                print(f"  {code} props:", list(data.get("properties",{}).keys()))
                print(f"  {code} additionalProperties:", data.get("additionalProperties"))
                if "$ref" in data:
                    print(f"  {code} ref:", data["$ref"])
                # if data wraps $ref
                for k,v in data.get("properties",{}).items():
                    if "$ref" in v:
                        print(f"    {k} -> {v['$ref']}")
                    if v.get("allOf"):
                        print(f"    {k} allOf {v['allOf']}")
        # error codes
        errs=[]
        for code, resp in op.get("responses",{}).items():
            if code.startswith("4") or code.startswith("5"):
                sch=resp.get("content",{}).get("application/json",{}).get("schema",{})
                props=sch.get("properties",{})
                code_enum=props.get("code",{}).get("enum")
                errs.append((code, code_enum))
        print("  ERRORS:", errs)
PY

with open(p) as f:
    d=json.load(f)

# dump each operation's request required fields and 200/201 data schema required+properties
for path, methods in d["paths"].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        if m.startswith("x-"): continue
        oid=op.get("operationId")
        print("="*80)
        print(f"{m.upper()} {path}  {oid}")
        rb=op.get("requestBody")
        if rb:
            content=rb.get("content",{}).get("application/json",{})
            sch=content.get("schema",{})
            print("  REQUEST required:", sch.get("required"))
            print("  REQUEST props:", list(sch.get("properties",{}).keys()))
            print("  additionalProperties:", sch.get("additionalProperties"))
        params=op.get("parameters")
        if params:
            print("  PARAMS:", [(p.get("name"), p.get("in"), p.get("required")) for p in params])
        for code in ["200","201","204"]:
            resp=op.get("responses",{}).get(code)
            if not resp: continue
            sch=resp.get("content",{}).get("application/json",{}).get("schema",{})
            if not sch: 
                print(f"  {code}: no schema")
                continue
            data=sch.get("properties",{}).get("data", sch)
            print(f"  {code} required:", data.get("required") if isinstance(data,dict) else data)
            if isinstance(data,dict):
                print(f"  {code} props:", list(data.get("properties",{}).keys()))
                print(f"  {code} additionalProperties:", data.get("additionalProperties"))
                if "$ref" in data:
                    print(f"  {code} ref:", data["$ref"])
                # if data wraps $ref
                for k,v in data.get("properties",{}).items():
                    if "$ref" in v:
                        print(f"    {k} -> {v['$ref']}")
                    if v.get("allOf"):
                        print(f"    {k} allOf {v['allOf']}")
        # error codes
        errs=[]
        for code, resp in op.get("responses",{}).items():
            if code.startswith("4") or code.startswith("5"):
                sch=resp.get("content",{}).get("application/json",{}).get("schema",{})
                props=sch.get("properties",{})
                code_enum=props.get("code",{}).get("enum")
                errs.append((code, code_enum))
        print("  ERRORS:", errs)
